title: FIGNA: Integer Unit-Based Accelerator Design for FP-INT GEMM Preserving Numerical Accuracy
problem: Weight-only quantization (INT weights with FP activations) in LLMs requires FP-INT multiply-accumulation operations, but these are currently performed on floating point units after dequantizing INT weights, lacking dedicated FP-INT arithmetic units that provide performance improvements.
motivation: Reducing computational burden and memory footprint of large language models through quantization while maintaining inference quality and performance.
method: FIGNA builds dedicated hardware that uses the integer arithmetic circuits already in processors to multiply floating-point numbers by integer numbers and add them together—exactly what happens when language models have their weights compressed to integers (quantized). By mapping floating-point operations onto integer operations, the design produces bit-for-bit identical results to traditional floating-point circuits, while being faster. The hardware flexibly supports different combinations of weight and activation precision levels for various quantized language model workloads.
key_novelty: Existing integer hardware in processors can perform FP-INT operations (multiplying a floating-point number by an integer) with exact numerical results, avoiding the approximations and model retraining that other methods require.
contributions: Demonstrates that dedicated FP-INT units do not yield substantial performance improvements over FPUs
Proposes FIGNA architecture using integer units for FP-INT MAC with exact numerical accuracy preservation
Achieves 6.34x higher TOPS/mm² and 2.19x higher TOPS/W compared to FPU baseline in FP16-INT4 case
Comprehensive evaluation on weight-only quantized LLMs (OPT, BLOOM) across multiple precision combinations

metrics.accuracy: Exact numerical accuracy preservation vs FPU

primary_theme: Integer-based accelerator for efficient FP-INT quantized LLM inference
